title: Microsoft Teams: admin recommendations to enable agents and apps for applications already in use
summary: Hold: the PowerShell example omits the operation required to assign users and groups. The instructions also omit the second admin centre required for tenants not yet using unified app management, and place the new recommendations on Manage apps without supporting documentation.

claims.claim: Administrators can discover and enable Teams agents corresponding to third-party applications already used in their organisation from Teams admin center.
claims.quote: For third-party applications already being used in your organization, admins can now discover and enable the corresponding Teams agents from within the Teams Admin Center.

claims.claim: The recommendations cover Teams apps as well as agents, with ServiceNow, Workday and Jira as examples of underlying applications.
claims.quote: Organizations often use third-party applications such as ServiceNow, Workday, Jira, and others, but the corresponding Microsoft Teams apps and agents may not be enabled for users.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes recommendations for high-value agents.
claims.quote: Admins receive recommendations for high-value agents

claims.claim: The roadmap promises visibility into required configuration changes during the enablement workflow.
claims.quote: gain visibility into any required configuration changes during the enablement workflow.

claims.claim: Usage signals prioritise the recommendations.
claims.quote: Recommendations are prioritized using usage signals

claims.claim: Administrators can make recommendations available to users already using the corresponding application.
claims.quote: Admins can choose to make a recommended app or agent available to users already using the corresponding application

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Administrators can target specific users and groups when enabling recommended apps or agents.
claims.quote: Admins must enable the feature and can target specific users or groups when enabling apps or agents.

claims.claim: Administrators can make a recommended app or agent available to everyone in the organisation.
claims.quote: Admins can choose to make a recommended app or agent available to users already using the corresponding application, specific users and groups, or everyone in the organization.

claims.claim: Administrators can choose to install a recommended app or agent for applicable users.
claims.quote: Admins can choose to install the app or agent for applicable users.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No enablement setting, UI path, PowerShell command or Graph equivalent for the recommendations feature is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams recommendations existing applications 569608 enable feature admin setting PowerShell Graph licensing sign-in signals. Read Learn manage-apps, app-centric-management, uam-tac-mac and Update-M365TeamsApp; no feature switch found.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated description of this recommendations feature at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams recommendations existing applications; Teams recommendations Manage apps existing. Read Learn manage-apps, app-centric-management and uam-tac-mac; results described other recommendations or the existing widget.

claims.claim: The existing Popular apps in your org widget on Manage apps shows most-used third-party apps not already installed for everyone.
claims.quote: you can see the Popular apps in your org widget on the Manage apps page. With this widget, you can see two of the most-used third-party apps that your users use the most, that aren't already installed for everyone in the organization.

claims.claim: The sources do not establish the relationship between the new recommendations and the existing Popular apps widget.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams recommendations Manage apps existing; Teams recommendations existing applications. Read MC1481316 and Learn app-centric-management and uam-tac-mac widget sections; none identifies the widget with roadmap item 569608.

claims.claim: App availability set to Everyone includes existing organisation users, new users and guests.
claims.quote: Everyone | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.claim: Specific users or groups excludes guests even if they are assigned.
claims.quote: Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.claim: The per-app availability UI is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Availability > Edit availability.
claims.quote:
Search for the required app and select the app name to open its app details page.
3. Select the Users and groups tab.
4. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability.
5. Select Edit availability.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -AppAssignmentType Everyone | UsersAndGroups [-Groups <groups>] [-Users <users>] is sufficient to manage app availability for everyone or selected users and groups.
claims.quote:
-OperationType
Operation performed on the app assigment.
Parameter sets
(Add
Mandatory: True
Remove)
Mandatory: True
claims.fix: Replace the shorthand with separate documented examples: 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -AppAssignmentType Everyone' and 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Users <users> -Groups <groups>'. Explain that Remove removes assignments and Noone is the no-user assignment type. Do not present a literal pipeline between assignment values.

claims.claim: Learn requires the Teams Administrator role to use Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role.

claims.claim: Higher-privilege administrators can also perform app governance tasks.
claims.quote: Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: Availability changes take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps controls bulk third-party app and agent availability.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. ... Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.

claims.claim: The org-wide toggle does not override apps whose availability was set individually.
claims.quote: This control doesn't override app-level configurations. ... The Org-wide app settings don't apply to: ... All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the org-wide Third-party apps toggle is documented in the references searched.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams org-wide app settings Graph; Teams org-wide third-party apps PowerShell. Read Learn manage-apps, app-centric-management, teamsAppSettings and Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration syntax; none documents automation of this toggle.

claims.claim: Learn states that third-party agents and apps are blocked by default in GCC.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how these recommendations interact with GCC's default block.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams recommendations existing applications 569608 enable feature admin setting PowerShell Graph licensing sign-in signals. Read MC1481316 and Learn manage-apps government section; no description of interaction with GCC's default block.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Some Teams apps require a separate service subscription.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality.

claims.claim: Making a paid third-party app available does not waive its service entitlement requirement.
claims.quote: Paid apps require users to authenticate to prevent unwarranted access. Also, user sign-in is required to check for entitlement and to make the corresponding app functionality available for the logged-in user.

claims.claim: Third-party apps and agents have developer terms and privacy policies describing their data handling.
claims.quote: In the terms of use and privacy policy of any agent or app, the app developer discloses what data their agent or app uses and how it handles the data.

claims.claim: The app details page in Teams admin center provides links to the developer's terms and privacy policy.
claims.quote: This information is available on app developer's website and you can access the URLs in the app details page in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: After unified app management migration, apps can be allowed in either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center's Integrated apps page and changes synchronise.
claims.quote: With unified agent app management, you can now manage agents and apps via the Teams admin center or Integrated apps page in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Any changes made in either admin center are automatically synchronized.

claims.where: Governance controls: instructions for applying existing availability controls
claims.claim: The instructions for making apps available through the existing controls apply without an additional step for tenants not migrated to unified app management.
claims.quote: If your organization isn't migrated to unified app management, allow apps and Copilot agents in Teams admin center and under the Integrated apps page in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.fix: Add the missing prerequisite beside the per-app availability instructions and in controls[1].note: 'If your organisation has not migrated to unified app management, allow the app or agent in both Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center > Integrated apps. After migration, either centre is sufficient.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management.

claims.claim: The new recommendations should be found on the Manage apps page.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams recommendations Manage apps existing. Read Learn manage-apps, app-centric-management and uam-tac-mac: only the existing widget is located there. MC1481316 names Teams admin center, not a page.
claims.fix: Replace 'Check the Manage apps page for the recommendations' with 'Check Teams admin center for the recommendations; Microsoft has not yet documented the page or enablement path.' Do not transfer the existing widget's location to the new feature.

claims.claim: Security groups and Microsoft 365 groups can be used to target app availability.
claims.quote: The supported group types are security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic user membership groups, nested groups, and the distribution lists.

claims.claim: The documented Users and groups tab can show both the number of users with availability and the actual number using an app.
claims.quote: The Users and groups tab opens, which shows the number of users for whom the selected app is available, and the actual number of users using the app.

claims.claim: The notice recommends communicating the change to administrators responsible for app governance and deployment.
claims.quote: Communicate the change to Teams administrators responsible for app governance and deployment.

claims.claim: MC1481316 recommends updating internal Teams app-management documentation where applicable.
claims.quote: Update any internal documentation related to Teams app management, if applicable.

claims.claim: A feature-specific administrator role or prerequisite beyond the surrounding Teams administration requirements is not stated.

claims.claim: The sources do not specify the sign-in signals' origin beyond application sign-ins, or where the signals are processed or stored.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams recommendations existing applications. Read roadmap, MC1481316 and Learn manage-apps; none specifies the capabilities of an individual recommended agent.

claims.claim: The feature targets Teams administrators managing app and agent deployment, while user access changes only through an administrator's availability or installation choice.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams administrators managing app and agent deployment ... Existing app availability and installation settings will not change unless an administrator takes action.
